title: Optical internal urethrotomy
subtitle: Wire across the stricture first, then cut at 12 o'clock under vision

sources.title: BAUS procedure-specific patient information and consent guidance

indications: A short (under about 2 cm) bulbar urethral stricture not previously treated, or a symptomatic recurrence where the patient declines urethroplasty.
contraindications: Long, dense, penile or multiple strictures, and failure of a previous urethrotomy (urethroplasty is better).
preparation: Retrograde and voiding urethrogram reviewed for length and site.
Consent: recurrence is common; bleeding, infection, erectile change, and self-calibration after.
positioning: Lithotomy, legs well supported and padded.
equipment: Urethrotome with a cold knife (Sachse), cystoscope, hydrophilic guidewire, fluoroscopy and contrast, catheters, suprapubic catheter set.
anatomy: Bulbar urethra, membranous urethra and the external sphincter, corpus spongiosum, the corpora cavernosa above the urethra.
criticalSafety: A guidewire passes through the stricture into the bladder before cutting.
Cut only at 12 o'clock and only scar.
structuresAtRisk: Corpus spongiosum and corpora (bleeding, erectile change)
commonErrors: Cutting without a wire and making a false passage.
Cutting deep into the corpus spongiosum.
complications: Erectile change, incontinence (if the sphincter is cut).
postop: Catheter for a short time per the surgeon.
Flow rate and symptom review; self-calibration if planned.
Refer for urethroplasty after a recurrence.

steps.emphasis: Urethroscopy to the stricture: note its site and look for a lumen.
Pass the wire through the stricture into the bladder and confirm it coils in the bladder on fluoroscopy.
A catheter over the wire into the bladder; write the removal date.
Record the stricture site and length, the cut, the catheter plan, and the urethroplasty discussion.

step.dviu.incise.title: Cold-knife incision at 12 o'clock
step.dviu.incise.why: Cutting the scar at 12 o'clock releases the narrowing with the least bleeding and keeps away from the rectum and the corpora at the sides.
how: With the wire in view, place the cold knife at 12 o'clock on the stricture.
Cut the scar in short strokes until healthy spongiosum and the lumen open and the scope passes easily into the bladder.
Inspect the bladder and confirm the urethra above the stricture is normal.
pitfalls: Cutting deep into the corpus spongiosum.
Extending the cut into the sphincter.

step.dviu.false-passage.title: Bailout: lost lumen or false passage
step.dviu.false-passage.why: A blind cut makes a false passage that turns a simple stricture into a complex one. If the lumen is lost, stop and divert urine.
how: If the wire will not pass or the scope leaves the lumen, stop cutting.
Place a suprapubic catheter and plan imaging and a formal urethroplasty.
Record exactly what happened and where.
